title: Merge sort & quick sort
learn: divide & conquer, merge step, partition (Lomuto/Hoare), O(n log n), quick sort worst case, stability, Python's Timsort
hook: "Sort an array without the built-in sort" is a real LeetCode problem and a common screen. Merge sort and quick sort are also the cleanest examples of divide and conquer you'll ever explain.

explain.prompt: Compare merge sort and quick sort: how each one works, their time and space complexity, and when quick sort degrades.
keyPoints: merge sort: split in half, sort both halves recursively, merge two sorted lists in linear time
log n levels × O(n) work per level = O(n log n) always; O(n) extra space; stable
quick sort: partition around a pivot (pivot lands in its final spot), recurse on both sides
O(n log n) average, O(n²) with consistently bad pivots (e.g. sorted input + last-element pivot); random pivot fixes it
quick sort is in place (O(log n) stack) but not stable
